notes.text: The late chapter paragraph names Tanhum bar Yirmeyah on starting with the preliminary prayer blessings.
The named Tanhum bar R. Yirmeyah interprets the names Asir and Shealtiel in the seal passage.
The exact patronymic and lemma introduce the teaching on four things that weaken strength.
Mana as teacher is directly attested in Gittin and the related narratives.
The twelve-mil wording is explicit in the direct passage.
The exact incident has Hefer, Tanhum bar Yirmeyah, Mana in Tzipporin and the twelve-mil rule. Sheviit 6:1:7 tells the parallel story with Tanhum bar Hiyya.
The extant homiletic parallel gives Nahum bar R. Yirmeyah, with the variant place form and Mani. Preserve the narrator’s equation as an attributed inference.
The parallel form Nahum is present; the equivalence remains attributed.
The Hefer and twelve-mil account agrees in broad structure; name forms differ between Gittin, Tanchuma and Sheviit. Editorial equation does not resolve identity.
